title: Active Brownian Dynamics in Channels: First-Passage and Spatiotemporal Properties via Siegmund Duality
summary: Accumulation at boundaries represents a widely observed phenomenon in active systems with implications for microbial ecology and engineering applications. To rationalize the underlying physics, we study the first-passage properties and spatial distributions of an active Brownian particle (ABP) in a channel. Leveraging Siegmund duality, we establish a direct mapping between the propagators of ABPs with absorbing and hard-wall boundary conditions, yielding analytical results in both problems.
